svg.title: K7 state change and rigid handling - mechanism close-ups
svg.desc: Six animated close-ups: sandwich press, cold cabinet, rigid handling and breading, bow knife, winding fork for Rouladen, slot washer.
svg.text: K7 mechanisms — how the state-change cell works
Soft food is made rigid in minutes; then a plain gantry, trays, a press and one knife can handle it.
Sandwich: flour, flatten in one stroke
Flour goes on BEFORE freezing (a frozen surface never gets
tacky). The platen stops on gauge rails 5 / 8 / 22 mm at 1 kN:
one stroke flattens, flours and gives good plate contact.
press platen down to the rails
Cold cabinet: fixed plates + loose cold slabs
5 fixed −25 °C plates, each with a loose 2.6 kg aluminium slab.
One comb lifts all slabs; trays slide in; slabs press down 100 N.
No refrigerant line moves; 21.5 kg Al stores the cold.
Rigid cutlet: handled like a part
A 1.5 s induction flash under T1 frees it from the tray. Rigid
at −5 °C it is held by ONE corner: dipped upright in egg, laid
in crumbs, tray shaken. It stays rigid for 5–10 minutes.
lid off, tongs at one corner
rigid: held by one corner, stays flat
Blade 0.6 × 12 × 200 in a C-bow (throat 270), ±6 mm at 45 Hz,
eccentric drive through a welded bellows. The gantry feeds the
pinned piece past the blade; slices fall one by one.
Two prongs 22 mm apart on the wrist axis: one under the meat
edge (board groove), one over the filling; 1.7 turns while X
follows. Seam ends down, frozen 6 mm deep (341 s), pin Ø 2.
Roulade board (cold tray with a cross groove)
fork out, roll stays seam down
Slot washer: flat ware in 70 s
Tray hung by its tab; a belt lift moves it between two facing
spray bars (6 flat fans each, 45 mm away). 70 s, 0.4 L, 40 Wh
per item; it leaves at 80 °C and dries by its own heat.
→ dry tray back to rack R
